items.t: Said Trump's actions are illegal and continue to raise prices for Arizona families.
items.q: Trump’s illegal actions continue to raise prices for Arizona families. Stay updated as we prove Trump and other administration officials are not above the law.

items.t: Supports Proposition 139, which enshrines the right to abortion in Arizona's constitution.
items.q: I want to thank the volunteers and organizers who worked tirelessly to bring this initiative to the ballot and secure its passage. Their dedication has ensured that the right to abortion is now enshrined in Arizona’s constitution.

items.t: Said OpenAI put Arizonans' safety at risk by failing to implement adequate user protections or transparency measures for minors using its chatbot.
items.q: Open AI put Arizonans safety at risk by failing to implement adequate user protections or transparency measures, despite clear indications that minors were regularly interacting with its chatbot.

items.t: Said firefighters should not be held in a job by a $15,000 payment requirement and that Arizona law does not allow such a penalty.
items.q: Firefighters run toward danger to protect our communities. They should not be trapped in a job by a $15,000 bill that bears no relationship to what their training actually costs,”

record.t: Joined a multistate coalition suing Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., HHS and other Trump administration officials over the dismantling of HHS.
record.q: Arizona, as part of a multistate coalition, filed a lawsuit challenging against Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr., the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services (HHS), and other Trump Administration officials to stop the dismantling of HHS.

record.t: Joined a coalition of 16 other states suing the Trump administration over states' access to Department of Education programs.
record.q: Arizona joined a coalition of 16 other states in suing the Trump administration to restore states’ access to critical Department of Education (ED) programs that support low-income and unhoused students

record.t: Joined a coalition of 19 states suing over Executive Order No. 14248 (the Elections Executive Order).
record.q: Arizona joined a coalition of 19 states in filing a lawsuit against President Donald J. Trump, U.S. Attorney General Pam Bondi, the federal Election Assistance Commission, and other Trump Administration officials over Executive Order No. 14248

record.t: Joined a coalition of 23 states suing HHS and Secretary Robert F. Kennedy Jr. over the termination of nearly $12 billion in public health grants.
record.q: Arizona joined a coalition of 23 states filing a lawsuit against the U.S. Department of Health and Human Services and HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy, Jr., for abruptly and illegally terminating nearly $12 billion in critical public health grants to the states.

record.t: Co-led a lawsuit with 11 other states challenging the delegation of executive power to Elon Musk.
record.q: Arizona co-led 11 other states in filing a lawsuit challenging the unlawful delegation of executive power to Elon Musk.

record.t: Joined a coalition of 19 attorneys general suing the Trump administration over access by Elon Musk and DOGE to the Treasury Department's central payment system.
record.q: Arizona joined a coalition of 19 attorneys general suing the Trump administration to stop the unauthorized disclosure of Arizonans’ private information and sensitive data.

record.t: Said she was investigating whether what Donald Trump said about Liz Cheney constituted a death threat under Arizona law (2024).
record.q: Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes told a local news outlet she was “investigating whether what Donald Trump said about Liz Cheney constituted a death threat under Arizona law.”

record.t: Was appointed to the Corporation Commission by Governor Janet Napolitano.
record.q: Kris Mayes was actually appointed to the Corporation Commission as a Republican (even if in name only) by then Democrat Gov. Janet Napolitano.

record.t: Announced a lawsuit against OpenAI alleging violations of the Arizona Consumer Fraud Act.
record.q: Attorney General Kris Mayes today announced that she is suing OpenAI for hurting Arizona children, deceiving parents, and violating Arizona laws. The complaint alleges widespread violations of the Arizona Consumer Fraud Act

record.t: Announced a lawsuit in Maricopa County Superior Court against the City of Tolleson over its firefighter training repayment policy.
record.q: Attorney General Kris Mayes today announced a lawsuit in Maricopa County Superior Court against the City of Tolleson, challenging a policy that requires newly hired entry-level firefighters to pay the City $15,000 if they leave within three years.
She is honored to serve as Arizona’s 27 th Attorney General, becoming the first mom and second woman ever to be elected to the office.

record.t: Served on the Arizona Corporation Commission.
record.q: During Mayes’ time on the Arizona Corporation Commission, her leadership helped create tens of thousands of high-paying jobs, saved Arizona consumers billions of dollars
